The Legend of Zelda. Nintendo's action-adventure franchise debuting in 1986, centered on the hero Link as he battles the sorcerer Ganon to save Princess Zelda and the kingdom of Hyrule. Known for intricate puzzle design, exploration, and the balance between combat and environmental problem-solving, the series defines the adventure-game genre. Zelda debuted on the Nintendo Entertainment System in 1986. The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past in 1991 on SNES cemented the formula of dungeons, keys, and interconnected exploration.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time in 1998 for Nintendo 64 revolutionized three-dimensional adventure gaming with dual-world mechanics featuring young and adult Link, lock-on combat, and cinematic scope. The series features a repeated cycle of incarnations. Link is reborn across millennia, as is Ganon and Princess Zelda, connected by the Triforce—three sacred golden triangles embodying Power, Wisdom, and Courage. Dungeons function as self-contained puzzle-boxes. Solving them yields keys, items, and maps that open new world areas, creating an interlocking world design model copied throughout the video game industry.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild in 2017 revolutionized open-world design with go-anywhere, tackle-anything-in-any-order freedom, minimal hand-holding, and environmental interactivity. Tears of the Kingdom in 2023 expands Breath of the Wild's engine with construction mechanics and a fully three-dimensional sky and underground world. The franchise spans handheld systems from Game Boy through DS, consoles from NES through SNES, N64, Wii, and Switch, and includes spin-offs like Cadence of Hyrule and Hyrule Warriors.

Link is the heroic avatar, reimagined across eras. Princess Zelda is the wise woman and namesake of the series, often more than just a rescue target. Ganon stands as incarnate evil, defeated yet eternally recurring. Hyrule is the fictional kingdom, rich with lore and geography. Nintendo, as publisher and architect of the adventure-game formula, has established a legacy that defined how adventure games are designed.
